# University of Edinburgh Summary
The University of Edinburgh boasts a rich history, tracing its origins to 1583 as Tounis College, which was established by a royal charter. Historically, it was a central hub of the Scottish Enlightenment, producing key figures such as Adam Smith and David Hume. The university is a member of the Russell Group and the Sutton 13 group, and it has historically been recognized for its medical school, whose graduates founded institutions at several Ivy League universities.
In terms of modern activities, the university has a diverse student life, featuring campaigning societies and the Edinburgh University Students' Association (EUSA). Student sports include participation in the Scottish Boat Race. The university is structured around three main colleges: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CAHSS), Science & Engineering (CSE), and Medicine & Vet Medicine (CMVM). It maintains several significant campus sites, including the Central Area, King's Buildings, the BioQuarter, and Easter Bush.
